answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake tokens to anchor each vertex within a dynamic interaction graph. Auditor collectives run topological cut verifications across clusters, penalizing colluding subgraphs via stake slashing when irregular clustering occurs. An attacker trying to anchor artificial identities at this computational wharf must stake compounding collateral, causing attacker cost to scale superlinearly. Failing audits dyes the node's umber reputation score permanently.
